From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Trellis MAP + evaluation hypotheses -> success criteria & exit checklist

Hi Alicia —

Thanks again for the time today. As promised, I pulled together a compact mutual action plan (MAP) draft and a first-pass set of evaluation hypotheses so we have a concrete acceptance runway for the Trellis pilot. Attached: Trellis-MAP-v0.2.xlsx and eval-test-cases-v1.pdf.

High-level intent: give both teams a single checklist of objective pass/fail tests plus the rollout timeline so Orson can validate against clinical SLAs and our delivery team can commit resources. Key sections in the MAP:

- Objective & success hypothesis (what success looks like for the pilot)
- Exit gates (hard failures that stop go/no-go)
- Acceptance tests (smoke + conformance + security artifacts)
- Measurement plan & owners (who runs each test and how often)
- Rollout cadence + signoff milestones (including canary and full cutover)

Proposed success signals (short):
- Functional: end-to-end recall on the prioritized 150 test prompts >= 92% (manual verification sample)
- Latency: 99th percentile inference latency under 350ms for the common request mix with our standard batch settings
- Stability: no more than one infra outage >3m during a 2-week evaluation window
- Safety/QA: no high-severity hallucination reports in the triage set (critical for clinical workflows)
- Integration: document-level fidelity (attachments/IDs) preserved in >=98% of cases when passed through the API

Exit gates (examples; any single one triggers pause-and-investigate):
- Failed encryption/KMS verification during key rotation test
- Repeated model regressions: >5% drop vs baseline on recall for anchor prompts
- Data leakage evidence (PII/exfiltration) in evaluation logs

Acceptance tests (by owner):
- Redwood QA: smoke generation suite + concurrency spike test (scripted)
- Orson devs: E2E clinical scenario checklist (10 high-risk vignettes)
- Security: KMS key-rotation and audit-log ingestion verification (security contact: marissa.cole)

Next steps I propose:
1) You review the MAP and the eval test cases (simple pass/fail table) — provide any must-have tests and the Orson signoff owners by Tue 11/17.
2) We lock the canary week (suggested 11/30–12/04) and schedule the joint readiness demo for 11/29.
3) Redwood runs the baseline run and shares a pre-flight checklist 48h before canary.

Quick ask: can you confirm the Orson security reviewer and a single tech contact who will run the E2E checklist items?

Attachments referenced inline: Trellis-MAP-v0.2.xlsx (MAP timeline + owners), eval-test-cases-v1.pdf (detailed test steps).

Thanks —
Soojin

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Trellis MAP + evaluation hypotheses -> success criteria & exit checklist

Thanks, Soojin — and for the clear template. A few quick clarifications from Orson's side: 

1) Security reviewer: that will be me (I own security for this engagement) and I'll loop in our infra lead (mike.lang@orsonhealth.com) if we need deeper logs access.
2) Clinical owner for E2E: Dr. Priya Natarajan (pri.natarajan@orsonhealth.com) will run the vignettes and sign E2E acceptance.
3) Latency requirement: 350ms at P99 is aggressive for our largest docs. Can we add a size-based tolerance: P99 <= 350ms for requests under 4k tokens; for >4k tokens, fallback P95 <= 1.2s?
4) For the data retention audit, we need proof that inference logs are retained for 90 days and that audit logs can be exported to our SIEM (we'll provide a sample ingestion schema).

A few suggested edits to the MAP: add a small section titled "Clinical safety evaluation" which lists 3 reviewers, their decision authority, and a rubric for what constitutes a high vs medium safety issue. Also would like the canary week to be 12/07–12/11 instead of the week you proposed to give our team time to prepare.

We reviewed the attachments — the eval-test-cases file is great but we'd like the smoke test matrix to explicitly call out the sample size for the recall check (we recommend at least 150 anchor prompts with randomized holdout).

I'll sign off on the security-related checklist items once we review the KMS rotation playbook (Marissa, can you share the KMS test steps we run?).

Thanks — Alicia
Alicia Cortez | Head of Security & Compliance, Orson Health
Alicia.Cortez@orsonhealth.com | +1 (212) 555-0199

Thanks for the good feedback, Alicia. A couple of operational notes and proposed additions to the MAP: 

- KMS rotation test steps: I'll attach a one-page playbook (summary) to the final MAP. The test will include: rotate key in staging, validate decrypt on a sample payload, verify audit event emitted to the audit-log topic, and confirm the old key is retired. Owner: Marissa Cole.
- Size-based latency tiers: agree with Alicia — updated the latency signal to include the two tiers (we'll document test payloads in the eval test cases).
- Clinical safety rubric: proposed three buckets (High: unsafe clinical recommendation, Medium: incorrect but non-actionable, Low: cosmetic phrasing issues). We'll require a single High to pause the pilot and convene a safety review within 24 hours.

I've edited the MAP spreadsheet (minor changes) and uploaded Trellis-MAP-v0.2.xlsx -> Trellis-MAP-v0.3-diff (will produce final v1 once Orson confirms). Ben and I also added a column for verification evidence (artifact name + link).

Proposed adjusted timeline (locked tentatively):
- 11/19: Orson returns must-have tests and owner names (Alicia/Dr. Priya)
- 11/30–12/04: Redwood baseline runs (non-production staging) + automated smoke (no PII ingestion)
- 12/07–12/11: Joint canary (production lite) — sample traffic, signoff on acceptance tests
- 12/13: Joint signoff window for final commitment (if all gates pass)

Action items I will take this week:
1) Create KMS playbook summary and attach to the MAP document.
2) Add the clinical safety rubric to the tests PDF.
3) Add evidence links for the baseline run script and test harness.

Ben — can you prepare the baseline throughput profile (qps, batch sizes, sequence length distribution) so we can include expected P99 numbers per size bucket?

Marissa
Marissa Cole | Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
